classification.difficultyReason: Multiply probabilities for four independent tosses and use a complementary event for at least one head.

content.prompt: A coin is tossed four times. What is the probability of:

answer.worked:
The tosses are independent, with probability $\frac12$ of a head on each toss.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{HHHH})&=\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\\P(\text{HHHH})&=\frac1{16}\end{align*}$$

The tosses are independent, with probability $\frac12$ of a tail on each toss.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{TTTT})&=\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\\P(\text{TTTT})&=\frac1{16}\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: head, tail, head, tail, in that order?

answer.worked:
Multiply the probabilities for the specified sequence of independent tosses.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{HTHT})&=\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\\P(\text{HTHT})&=\frac1{16}\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: heads in the first three tosses but not in the fourth?

answer.worked:
The required sequence is HHHT. The tosses are independent.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{HHHT})&=\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\times\frac12\\P(\text{HHHT})&=\frac1{16}\end{align*}$$

children.label: e
children.prompt: a head in at least one of the four tosses?

answer.short:
$\frac{15}{16}$

Use the complement of four tails.
answer.worked:
The complement of at least one head is four tails.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one head})&=1-P(\text{TTTT})\\P(\text{at least one head})&=1-\left(\frac12\right)^4\\P(\text{at least one head})&=1-\frac1{16}\\P(\text{at least one head})&=\frac{15}{16}\end{align*}$$
